chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Mahbub from Ibrahim al-Kharqiyyi said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The testimony of women is valid in what men cannot see and testify about; their testimony is valid in marriage, but not valid in divorce and not valid in blood (diyah); it is valid in the punishment for fornication if there are three men and two women, and it is not valid if there are two men and four women in stoning.'
ai.seo_question: When is the testimony of women considered valid in Shia Islamic law?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the juristic distinction between civil and penal testimonies, noting that while women's testimony is valid in marriage (*nikah*) and private matters, it is excluded from divorce (*talaq*) and blood money (*diyah*). It further specifies the variable ratios of male to female witnesses required for the punishment of fornication (*hadd*) versus stoning (*rajm*), reflecting the nuanced application of Quranic principles in Shia fiqh. This hadith serves as a key reference for understanding how Shia scholars interpret the flexibility of witness requirements based on the nature of the legal proceeding.
